note: Re-judged 2026-10-30 (independent auditor) after the user-namespace conversion (25fbb6e890/d8427e4380): the TestVRRPOwnerAnswersWithVirtualMACOnly and TestVRRPNonOwnerMasterAnswersARPWithVirtualMACOnly unit gained only `if !userns.Enter(t) { return }` as its first statement and its build tag moved from integration&&linux to linux. userns.Enter (internal/test/userns/userns_linux.go) re-runs the one named test in a fresh user+net+mount namespace and returns false to the parent only when the child reported PASS or SKIP; a failing child, a non-zero exit, or a child that ran nothing calls t.Fatalf, so every assertion below the guard still fails the test when the behaviour breaks. Body otherwise byte-identical. RFC 3768 Section 8.2: "The Master virtual router MUST NOT respond with its physical MAC address." Fresh judgement: owner case, with the owner filter every ARP reply carries the virtual MAC and none the physical one, against a control where the parent answers with its physical MAC and a withdrawal that restores it; non-owner case, the product recipe removes the physical-MAC answer seen in the control. Enforced.
